 Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Increase: How Much Is Projected for 2027 
 The Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) is one of the most important tax benefits for low- and moderate-income workers because it can translate into a direct cash refund . Each year, its maximum amount is adjusted for inflation , and a new increase is projected for 2027.

 The EITC is a tax credit designed to reward and help people who work and earn low or moderate incomes . Its big advantage is that it is refundable : that means if the credit is greater than the taxes a person owes, the difference is returned as a refund. In other words, a worker can end up receiving money from the IRS even if their tax bill is low or zero.
 The amount each person actually receives depends on three factors : their income, their filing status, and the number of qualifying children. So the projected maximum is a ceiling: not everyone receives that amount, but rather the amount that applies to their situation.
 Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Increase: How Much Is Projected for 2027
 The EITC amount depends on the number of qualifying children . These are the confirmed maximum amounts for 2026 and the projected amounts for 2027:
 No children : from $664 (confirmed for 2026) to about $680 (projected for 2027). 
 One child : from $4,427 to about $4,538. 
 Two children : from $7,316 to about $7,499. 
 Three or more children : from $8,231 to about $8,400. 
 The IRS updates EITC amounts every year in a document called a Revenue Procedure , which it usually publishes between October and November . As of this report, the official figures for 2027 have not yet been released. 
 That is why the numbers being used are estimates based on inflation , and they may differ by a few dollars from the final figure announced by the agency.
